name: Edge-Protected Public Service
description: A pattern for public-facing services that require robust edge protection including DDoS mitigation, web application firewall, bot management, and CDN caching. Designed for high-profile government services that are frequent targets for cyber attacks and must maintain availability under adversarial conditions.
whenToUse: High-profile public services that are likely targets for DDoS or application-layer attacks
Services handling sensitive citizen data that require defence-in-depth at the network edge
Public APIs exposed to the internet requiring rate limiting and abuse prevention
Services where availability must be maintained during active cyber attacks
Government services following NCSC Secure by Design principles for internet-facing systems
whenNotToUse: Internal-only services not exposed to the public internet
Low-profile services with minimal attack surface and low risk profile
Services behind VPN or corporate network that are not internet-accessible
Development and testing environments where edge protection adds unnecessary cost
Simple static websites with no dynamic content or user data

typicalComponents.name: DDoS Protection
typicalComponents.purpose: Absorb and mitigate volumetric and protocol-level DDoS attacks
typicalComponents.technology: AWS Shield Advanced, Azure DDoS Protection, or Cloud Armor

typicalComponents.name: Web Application Firewall
typicalComponents.purpose: Inspect and filter HTTP traffic for application-layer attacks
typicalComponents.technology: AWS WAF, Azure WAF, or Cloud Armor WAF

typicalComponents.name: CDN with Edge Caching
typicalComponents.purpose: Cache content at edge locations to reduce origin load and improve performance
typicalComponents.technology: CloudFront, Azure Front Door, or Cloud CDN

typicalComponents.name: Bot Management
typicalComponents.purpose: Detect and block automated bot traffic while allowing legitimate crawlers
typicalComponents.technology: AWS WAF Bot Control, Azure Bot Protection, or reCAPTCHA Enterprise

typicalComponents.name: Origin Protection
typicalComponents.purpose: Ensure origin servers only accept traffic from the CDN/WAF layer
typicalComponents.technology: Origin Access Identity, Private Link, or IAP

securityControls: Implement layered DDoS protection at network (L3/L4) and application (L7) layers
Configure WAF rules for OWASP Top 10 protection with custom rules for application-specific threats
Implement rate limiting per IP and per authenticated user to prevent abuse
Use geo-blocking to restrict access from countries where the service has no legitimate users
Implement TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites and certificate pinning where appropriate
Enable real-time security event logging and integrate with SIEM for threat detection
Implement CAPTCHA or proof-of-work challenges for suspicious traffic patterns
resilienceConsiderations: Edge protection services are globally distributed and inherently resilient
CDN caching can serve content even if origin is temporarily unavailable
DDoS protection absorbs attack traffic before it reaches application infrastructure
Implement origin failover for scenarios where primary origin becomes unreachable
Design rate limiting to protect the service without blocking legitimate users during peaks
Regular testing of WAF rules to ensure they don't block legitimate traffic
costConsiderations: DDoS protection services have fixed monthly costs plus per-incident charges
WAF costs scale with request volume and number of rules evaluated
CDN costs based on data transfer and request volume
Advanced bot management features carry premium pricing
Consider the cost of a successful attack (downtime, data breach) versus protection costs
Shield Advanced (AWS) includes DDoS cost protection for scaling during attacks
operationalConsiderations: WAF rules require ongoing tuning to balance security with false positive rates
Security operations team must monitor and respond to edge security alerts
Regular review of blocked traffic to identify false positives and legitimate users affected
Incident response procedures for active DDoS attacks
Coordination with NCSC for threat intelligence and attack response
Regular penetration testing to validate edge protection effectiveness

services.name: AWS Shield Advanced
services.purpose: Managed DDoS protection with 24/7 response team

services.name: AWS WAF
services.purpose: Web application firewall with managed rule groups

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.purpose: CDN with integrated WAF and DDoS protection

questionsToAsk: What is the threat profile for this service — is it a likely target for state-sponsored or hacktivist attacks?
What is the acceptable false positive rate for WAF rules blocking legitimate users?
Is there an existing relationship with NCSC for threat intelligence sharing?
What is the expected legitimate traffic volume and how does it differ from attack patterns?
Are there geographic restrictions on where the service should be accessible?
What is the incident response process for active cyber attacks?
commonMistakes: Deploying WAF with default rules only and never tuning for the specific application
Not testing WAF rules against legitimate traffic, causing false positives that block real users
Exposing origin servers directly, allowing attackers to bypass edge protection
Not implementing rate limiting, allowing application-layer attacks to exhaust resources
Treating edge protection as set-and-forget rather than continuously monitoring and tuning
